mainTopic: Corrupt judges and redemption; רבי מלאי's אגדות; רב מנשיא's answers to the people of בשכר
overview: The amud opens with the last words of a teaching from the previous page: a time will come when no one finds a clear הלכה and a clear משנה in one place. A ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן אלישע then teaches that troubles come to the world because of corrupt judges, and that the שכינה will not return until they are removed. It proves this from פסוקים in מיכה and ישעיהו. עולא, רב פפא, and other אמוראים add teachings on the same theme: redemption comes through צדקה, fixing ourselves removes foreign oppressors, and everyone in a corrupt court shares the blame. A string of teachings by רבי מלאי follows: יוסף did not drink wine after leaving his brothers, the brothers' own drinking is discussed, and אהרן earned the חושן because he was glad at משה's greatness. The גמרא then returns to הלכה with three questions the people of בשכר sent to לוי. After לוי dies, רב מנשיא answers them strictly about a כילה on שבת and about hops in a vineyard, and he holds back real leniencies because the questioners were not learned. The amud ends with his strict ruling about burying a מת on יום טוב, and the start of a challenge from a story in מעון that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the prediction that clear Torah knowledge will be hard to find
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of a teaching from the previous page: no one will find a clear הלכה and a clear משנה in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: …a clear הלכה and a clear teaching in one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence it started on the previous page. That sentence described a future time when Torah would be confused and hard to find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full teaching says that people will search for Torah but will not find a clear ruling and a clear source together in one place. In other words, there will be disputes and uncertainty among the חכמים. This line simply completes that thought before a new ברייתא begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear, settled teaching or source
In one place, meaning together without dispute

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the tail end of a sentence that began on the previous page, so do not read it as a standalone statement.

phrases.english: a clear halakha and a clear teaching
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from the previous page: they will not find…

phrases.english: in one place.
phrases.notes: There will be disputes rather than clarity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה בְּרוּרָה וּמִשְׁנָה בְּרוּרָה בִּמְקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a teaching begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A time will come when clear rulings and clear sources will not be found together.

steps.title: When troubles come, examine the judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן אלישע teaches that if a generation suffers many troubles, the cause should be looked for in the judges of Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי בן אלישע says: If you see a generation upon which many troubles are coming, go and examine the judges of Israel. For every calamity that comes to the world comes only because of the judges of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא. רבי יוסי בן אלישע teaches that the judges of Israel are the source of a generation's troubles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is strong: calamity comes only because of the judges. When judges are corrupt, justice in society breaks down, and punishment follows for everyone. The next step brings a פסוק to prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei ben Elisha says:
If you see a generation
that many troubles are coming upon it —
go and examine the judges of Israel.
For every calamity that comes to the world

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּאָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל דַּיָּינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: comes only because of the judges of Israel,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on a related theme: the breakdown of Torah and justice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calamity comes to the world because of corrupt judges of Israel.

steps.title: Proof from מיכה about corrupt leaders
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves its claim from מיכה, who condemns leaders who pervert justice, take bribes, and still say they rely on ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is stated: 'Hear this, heads of the house of Jacob and officers of the house of Israel, who abhor justice and twist all that is straight; who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with iniquity. Her heads judge for bribes, her priests teach for a price, her prophets divine for money, yet they lean on the Lord…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove that the leaders and judges cause the destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא lists the sins of the leaders: they hate justice, build the city through bloodshed, and take bribes. He names three corrupt groups: heads who judge for bribes, priests who rule for a price, and prophets who divine for money. The phrase about leaning on ה׳ sets up the next comment in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: They lean on or rely upon

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שִׁמְעוּ נָא זֹאת רָאשֵׁי בֵּית יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Hear this, heads of the house of Jacob'
and officers of the house of Israel
who abhor justice
and pervert all that is straight;
who build Zion with blood
and Jerusalem with iniquity.
Her heads judge for bribes,
phrases.notes: Sin #1

phrases.english: and her priests teach for a price,
phrases.notes: Sin #2

phrases.english: and her prophets divine for money,
phrases.notes: Sin #3

phrases.english: yet they lean on the Lord, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: שִׁמְעוּ נָא זֹאת רָאשֵׁי בֵּית יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for רבי יוסי בן אלישע's claim
steps.raayaObject: That calamity comes because of corrupt judges and leaders

steps.title: Wicked, yet trusting in ה׳
steps.stepSummary: Explaining the end of the פסוק, the גמרא says these leaders were wicked but still placed their trust in ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are wicked, but they placed their trust in the One Who spoke and the world came into being.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comments on the phrase 'yet they lean on the Lord.' This comment sets up the next step about their punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These leaders were truly wicked, yet they relied on ה׳ to protect them. The גמרא points out this mix of corruption and faith. It then explains how ה׳ dealt with them.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who spoke and the world came into being, meaning ה׳

phrases.english: They are wicked,
but they placed their trust
in the One Who spoke and the world came into being.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interprets the closing words of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The corrupt leaders were wicked, yet they trusted in ה׳.

steps.title: Three punishments for three sins
steps.stepSummary: Because of this, ה׳ brings three punishments that match the three sins, as the next פסוק in מיכה describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings upon them three calamities corresponding to the three sins in their hands, as it is stated: 'Therefore, because of you, Zion shall be plowed as a field, Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the Temple Mount like the high places of a forest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the next פסוק describes exactly three punishments. These match the three sins listed earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three sins were judges taking bribes, priests ruling for a price, and prophets divining for money. The three punishments are Zion plowed, Jerusalem in ruins, and the Temple Mount overgrown like a forest. The punishment matches the sin measure for measure. Their trust in ה׳ did not cancel the punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: Three corrupt groups (judges, priests, prophets) led to three punishments (Zion, Jerusalem, Temple Mount), measure for measure.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, מֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהֶן
phrases.english: Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings upon them
three calamities
corresponding to the three sins in their hands,
phrases.notes: Bribes, payment for rulings, payment for prophecy

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Therefore, because of you'
Zion shall be plowed as a field,
phrases.notes: Punishment #1

phrases.english: and Jerusalem shall become heaps,
phrases.notes: Punishment #2

phrases.english: and the Temple Mount like the high places of a forest.'
phrases.notes: Punishment #3

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִיכָךְ, מֵבִיא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ פּוּרְעָנִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the consequence and proves it from the next פסוק (מיכה ג:יב)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sins of the leaders bring three corresponding punishments.

steps.title: The שכינה returns only when corrupt judges are gone
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ will not rest His שכינה on Israel until wicked judges and officers are removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not rest His Divine Presence upon Israel until wicked judges and officers cease from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a final teaching: the שכינה depends on getting rid of corrupt judges and officers. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained that corrupt judges bring destruction. This step gives the positive side: redemption and the return of the שכינה require removing them. Justice is the precondition for ה׳'s presence.

keyTerms.meaning: That they will cease or be eliminated

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not rest His Divine Presence upon Israel

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ שׁוֹפְטִים וְשׁוֹטְרִים רָעִים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: until wicked judges and officers cease from Israel,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַשְׁרֶה שְׁכִינָתוֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the cause of destruction to the condition for redemption
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה will not rest on Israel until corrupt judges and officers are removed.

steps.title: Proof from ישעיהו: purging the dross and restoring judges
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from ישעיהו: ה׳ will purge Israel's impurities and restore its judges as at first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is stated: 'I will turn My hand upon you, purge away your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy. And I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning…'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the previous step from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purging the dross means removing the corrupt leaders. Only after that will the righteous judges be restored, and the פסוק goes on to say the city will be called righteous. So the removal of bad judges comes before restoration.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will refine or purge
Your alloy, the mixed-in base metals

steps.whatToRemember: Corrupt judges bring destruction (מיכה), and only their removal brings back the שכינה (ישעיהו). The quality of a nation's judges determines its fate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא places the moral weight of national well-being on the integrity of its judges and leaders.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'And I will turn My hand upon you'
and purge away your dross as with lye
and remove all your alloy.
And I will restore your judges as at first
and your counselors as at the beginning, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural proof for step 6
steps.raayaObject: That the שכינה returns only after corrupt judges are removed

steps.title: Jerusalem will be redeemed only through righteousness
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that ירושלים will be redeemed only through צדקה, citing ישעיהו 1:27.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Jerusalem will be redeemed only through righteousness, as it says: 'Zion will be redeemed with justice, and those who return to her with righteousness.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a new teaching: the redemption of ירושלים depends on צדקה. He proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק he quotes comes right after the one in Step 7 about restoring the judges. So the flow is clear: first honest judges (משפט) return, and then redemption comes through צדקה. עולא focuses on the second half of the פסוק, 'with righteousness,' and says it is the necessary condition for redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often traveled between ארץ ישראל and בבל
Those who return to her (her returnees, or her penitents)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גמרא links national redemption to how the people behave, both justice in court and צדקה in society.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Jerusalem is not redeemed
except through righteousness,
as it is said: 'Zion will be redeemed with justice'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:27, the very next פסוק after the one cited in Step 7

phrases.english: 'and those who return to her with righteousness.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אֵין יְרוּשָׁלָיִם נִפְדֵּית אֶלָּא בִּצְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same passage in ישעיהו (1:26 to 1:27), moving from restoring judges to the condition for redemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים will be redeemed only through צדקה.

steps.title: When the arrogant and corrupt judges disappear, the oppressors disappear too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא teaches two parallel rules. When the arrogant cease, the אמגושי cease. When corrupt judges cease, the גזירפטי cease.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If the arrogant cease to exist, the fire priests will cease. If the corrupt judges cease, the royal officers will cease.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא states two parallel 'if-then' rules about how Israel's own faults bring foreign oppressors. He will prove each half in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is measure for measure. Israel's internal sins are matched by outside oppressors. Arrogance among Jews brings the domineering Persian fire priests, and corrupt Jewish judges bring the harsh government officers. Remove the internal sin, and the external punishment goes away with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Persian fire priests (magi) who persecuted Jews
Royal officers or taskmasters who oppressed the people

steps.confusionAlert: The arrogant people and the corrupt judges here are Jews. The אמגושי and גזירפטי are foreign oppressors. The point is that fixing ourselves removes the outside enemy.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If the arrogant cease —
the fire priests will cease.
If the corrupt judges cease —
the royal officers will cease.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי בָּטְלִי יְהִירֵי בָּטְלִי אַמְגּוּשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the theme that removing corruption within Israel brings relief and redemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Internal arrogance and corrupt justice bring matching foreign oppressors, and removing them removes the oppressors.

steps.title: Proof that removing the arrogant removes the fire priests
steps.stepSummary: The first half of רב פפא's teaching is proven from ישעיהו 1:25: 'I will purge away your dross as with lye.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If the arrogant cease, the fire priests cease': as it is written, 'And I will purge away your dross as with lye.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first half of רב פפא's statement and gives its source in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'dross' (סיגיך) is read as the arrogant within Israel. The rest of the פסוק, 'and I will remove all your alloy (בדיליך),' is read as the fire priests, who are separated from the fear of ה׳. Both are removed together, so when one goes, the other goes too.

keyTerms.meaning: Your dross, read as the arrogant

phrases.english: If the arrogant cease, the fire priests cease —
as it is written: 'And I will purge away your dross as with lye.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:25. The proof really comes from the next words of the פסוק, 'ואסירה כל בדיליך.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּטְלִי יְהִירֵי בָּטְלִי אַמְגּוּשֵׁי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the first half of Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Removing the arrogant leads to removing the אמגושי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 1:25: dross (arrogant) and alloy (fire priests) are purged together.

steps.title: Proof that removing corrupt judges removes the oppressive officers
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רב פפא's teaching is proven from צפניה 3:15: 'ה׳ has removed your judgments, cleared away your enemy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If the corrupt judges cease, the royal officers cease': as it is written, 'The Lord has removed your judgments, He has cleared away your enemy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the second half of רב פפא's statement and proves it from a פסוק. This finishes the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Removed your judgments' is read as removing the corrupt judges. Right after it comes 'cleared away your enemy,' meaning the oppressive officers. The two clauses sit side by side, showing that one leads straight to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Your judgments, read as your corrupt judges

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section teaches one idea. The שכינה, redemption, and freedom from oppressors all depend on Israel fixing its own justice, humility, and צדקה. Corrupt judges and arrogance bring matching foreign oppressors.

phrases.english: If the corrupt judges cease, the royal officers cease —
as it is written: 'The Lord has removed your judgments,'
phrases.notes: צפניה 3:15

phrases.english: 'He has cleared away your enemy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּטְלִי דַּיָּינֵי בָּטְלִי גְּזִירְפָּטֵי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 10. It supplies the source for the second half of Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Removing corrupt judges leads to removing the גזירפטי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: צפניה 3:15: removal of 'your judgments' is immediately followed by clearing away 'your enemy.'

steps.title: Reading 'The staff of the wicked' as corrupt judges and their protectors
steps.stepSummary: רבי מלאי, quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, explains ישעיהו 14:5. The 'staff of the wicked' means judges who back their abusive attendants. The 'rod of the rulers' means the תלמידי חכמים in the judges' families who cover for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מלאי said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: What is the meaning of the verse 'ה׳ has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers'? 'ה׳ has broken the staff of the wicked' means the judges who became a stick for their attendants. 'The rod of the rulers' means the תלמידי חכמים who belong to the judges' families.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher explains a verse in ישעיהו. He applies each half of it to a different group of people involved in a corrupt justice system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'staff' is the judges. They give their attendants the power and backing to bully people. The 'rod' is the scholars from the judges' families, who use their standing to protect their relatives. The point is that ה׳ will break both the corrupt judges and the people who support them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (a formula that opens the explanation of a verse)
Their attendants (court officers who carry out the judges' orders)
A stick or staff, meaning a source of force and backing

steps.confusionAlert: Here חזן does not mean a cantor. In this context it means a court attendant or officer who enforces the judges' rulings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mallai said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:5

phrases.english: the rod of the rulers.'
'The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked':
these are the judges
who became a staff for their attendants.
phrases.notes: The judges give backing to attendants who abuse people.

phrases.english: 'The rod of the rulers':
these are the Torah scholars
who are in the families of the judges.
phrases.notes: They use their prestige to cover up for their relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מַלַּאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of corrupt judges from רב פפא's teaching, now with a new verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ישעיהו 14:5, the 'staff of the wicked' is the judges who back their abusive attendants, and the 'rod of the rulers' is the scholars in the judges' families who protect them.

steps.title: Mar Zutra's different reading of 'the rod of the rulers'
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the 'rod of the rulers' means scholars who teach just enough public laws to ignorant judges so they can keep their posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: These are the תלמידי חכמים who teach public הלכות to ignorant judges.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers a different explanation of the second half of the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the scholars sin because of family loyalty. Here they sin by coaching ignorant judges in the public-facing laws, so nobody notices the judges know nothing. Either way, these scholars hold up a corrupt court.

keyTerms.meaning: Public or communal laws, the basic rules a judge shows in public
Ignorant judges who do not really know Torah

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
These are the Torah scholars
who teach communal laws
to ignorant judges.
phrases.notes: This lets the ignorant judges hide their ignorance and keep their positions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative explanation of 'שבט מושלים' from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'rod of the rulers' is scholars who coach ignorant judges in public laws so they can stay in power.

steps.title: Four body parts in the verse, four players in a corrupt court
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן מלאי, quoting ריש לקיש, explains ישעיהו 59:3. Hands are the judges, fingers are their scribes, lips are their legal advisors, and the tongue is the litigants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן מלאי said in the name of ריש לקיש: What is the meaning of the verse 'For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, your tongue utters wickedness'? 'Your hands are defiled with blood' means the judges. 'Your fingers with iniquity' means the judges' scribes. 'Your lips have spoken lies' means the judges' advisors. 'Your tongue utters wickedness' means the litigants.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teacher quotes a verse with four parts and assigns each part to a different person in a corrupt courtroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hands match the judges, who take bribes with their hands. Fingers match the scribes, who write false documents. Lips match the advisors, who give dishonest arguments. The tongue matches the litigants, who lie in their own cases. The verse is read as blaming everyone in the courtroom, not only the judges.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges' scribes, who write up court documents
Legal advisors or advocates who argue cases before the judges
The litigants, meaning the two sides in a court case

steps.whatToRemember: This whole section blames the entire justice system: judges, attendants, protective scholars, scribes, advisors, and even the litigants themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Mallai said
in the name of Reish Lakish:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'For your hands are defiled with blood
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 59:3

phrases.english: and your fingers with iniquity;
your lips have spoken lies,
your tongue utters wickedness.'
'For your hands are defiled with blood':
these are the judges.
phrases.notes: They take bribes in their hands.

phrases.english: 'And your fingers with iniquity':
these are the scribes of the judges.
phrases.notes: They write falsehood with their fingers.

phrases.english: 'Your lips have spoken lies':
these are the legal advisors of the judges.
'Your tongue utters wickedness':
these are the litigants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן מַלַּאי מִשּׁוּם רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second verse on the same theme of corrupt courts, widening the blame to everyone involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ישעיהו 59:3, hands are the judges, fingers are the scribes, lips are the advisors, and the tongue is the litigants.

steps.title: יוסף drank no wine after leaving his brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבי מלאי, quoting רבי יצחק מגדלאה, teaches that from the day יוסף was separated from his brothers, he did not taste wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מלאי said in the name of רבי יצחק מגדלאה: From the day that יוסף separated from his brothers, he did not taste the taste of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching by the same רבי מלאי, on a different subject: יוסף's conduct after he was sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic changes because the teachings are collected by teacher, not by subject. רבי מלאי was just quoted in step 12, so another of his statements is brought here. The claim is that יוסף held back from wine for all his years apart from his brothers. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not taste even the taste of wine

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a link to corrupt judges here. The connection is that the same teacher, רבי מלאי, is being quoted, as the word 'וְאָמַר' ('and he also said') shows.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Mallai said
in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak from Migdal:
From the day that Yosef parted from his brothers
he did not taste the taste of wine,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי מַלַּאי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִצְחָק מַגְדְּלָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked only because the same teacher, רבי מלאי, is quoted again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף abstained from wine from the time he was separated from his brothers.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'נזיר' in יעקב's blessing
steps.stepSummary: The proof is בראשית 49:26, where יוסף is called 'נזיר אחיו'. The word נזיר suggests he lived like a נזיר, who does not drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And on the crown of the head of the נזיר of his brothers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the verse that proves רבי מלאי's claim about יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, 'נזיר אחיו' means 'the one separated from his brothers.' The word נזיר also calls to mind a נזיר, whose main restriction is not drinking wine. So the verse hints that יוסף acted like a נזיר while he was apart from his brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is separated, or a נזיר who abstains from wine

steps.whatToRemember: The proof depends on the double meaning of נזיר: 'separated' and 'one who refrains from wine.'

phrases.english: as it is written: 'and on the crown of the head of the one separated [nazir] from his brothers.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:26, יעקב's blessing to יוסף

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse proof for the claim in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That יוסף abstained from wine after being separated from his brothers
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 49:26: 'ולקדקד נזיר אחיו', reading נזיר as hinting at a נזיר who abstains from wine

steps.title: The brothers also did not drink wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the brothers of יוסף also did not taste wine during the years they were separated from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: They, too, did not taste the taste of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds to רבי מלאי's teaching. רבי מלאי said only יוסף stopped drinking wine, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the brothers stopped too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' ('also') shows that he accepts what was said about יוסף and adds the brothers. The brothers felt guilty about selling יוסף, so they held back from wine too. His proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הֵן לֹא טָעֲמוּ טַעַם יַיִן,
phrases.english: they too did not taste the taste of wine,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the brothers of יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: אַף הֵן לֹא טָעֲמוּ טַעַם יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the brothers to רבי מלאי's statement about יוסף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brothers, like יוסף, did not drink wine during the years of separation.

steps.title: Proof from 'they drank and became drunk with him'
steps.stepSummary: The proof is בראשית 43:34. When the brothers ate with יוסף, they 'drank and became drunk with him,' which implies they had not been drinking until then.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they drank and became drunk with him.' We can infer that until now there was no drunkenness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's proof from a verse. It describes the brothers drinking at the meal when they met יוסף again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse stresses that they drank 'with him,' meaning on that day. This suggests it was something new, so before that day they did not drink wine at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And they drank and became drunk with him (בראשית 43:34)

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And they drank and became drunk with him,'
by implication, until now
there was no drunkenness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for Step 17
steps.raayaObject: That the brothers did not drink wine during the separation
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 43:34, 'וישתו וישכרו עמו', read as implying that before this they did not drink

steps.title: How רבי מלאי reads the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion, רבי מלאי, says the verse only shows the brothers had not gotten drunk until then. They did still drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? It was drunkenness that there was not, but drinking there was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי מלאי, who said only יוסף avoided wine, deals with this verse. It answers that the verse only teaches the brothers had not been drunk, not that they had not drunk at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step blocks the proof in Step 18. The new thing the verse describes is getting drunk, not drinking. So the brothers drank wine in small amounts but never got drunk, and only יוסף fully gave up wine.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion), how does he explain it?

steps.confusionAlert: 'ואידך' here refers to רבי מלאי from Step 15, not to someone new. He holds that only יוסף stopped drinking wine.

phrases.english: And the other one? It was drunkenness that there was not,
but drinking, at least, there was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי מלאי is not forced to accept the proof of Step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the conclusion that the brothers avoided wine entirely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse implies only that the brothers were not drunk before, not that they never drank.

steps.title: אהרן earned the breastplate because he was glad for משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מלאי teaches that because אהרן was truly happy in his heart when משה became the leader, he earned the right to wear the חושן המשפט on his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מלאי said: As a reward for 'and he will see you and be glad in his heart,' he earned the breastplate of judgment on his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אגדה teaching from רבי מלאי, connected to the same theme of how brothers treat each other. אהרן was not jealous of his younger brother משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward matches the good deed. אהרן's heart was full of real joy, so the holy חושן, worn by the כהן גדול, rests on his heart (שמות 4:14 and שמות 28:30).

keyTerms.meaning: And he will see you and be glad in his heart (שמות 4:14)
The breastplate of judgment worn by the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: The אגדה section ends here. Being truly happy for someone else's success, as אהרן was, is rewarded measure for measure.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Mallai said:
as a reward for 'and he will see you and be glad in his heart,'
he earned the breastplate of judgment upon his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר רַבִּי מַלַּאי: בִּשְׂכַר ״וְרָאֲךָ וְשָׂמַח בְּלִבּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי מלאי on how brothers related to each other
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן earned the חושן on his heart as a reward for his heartfelt joy at משה's greatness.

steps.title: The people of בשכר send three questions to לוי
steps.stepSummary: The people of בשכר ask לוי three halachic questions: about a כילה on שבת, about hops in a vineyard, and about a person who dies on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of בשכר sent to לוי: A canopy, what is the law? Hops in a vineyard, what is the law? A dead person on a festival, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to הלכה and the topic of the כילה (canopy). A town sends לוי three practical questions, and the answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question is a real practical problem. The first asks whether one may spread a canopy on שבת, or whether that counts as making a tent. The second asks whether hops growing in a vineyard count as forbidden כלאים. The third asks how to handle the burial of someone who dies on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of the town of בשכר

phrases.english: The people of Bashkar sent to Levi:
A canopy, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Spreading it on שבת.

phrases.english: Hops in a vineyard, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Is it כלאים?

phrases.english: A dead person on a festival, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the halachic topic of the canopy
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law about spreading a canopy on שבת, hops in a vineyard, and a person who dies on יום טוב

steps.title: לוי dies, and שמואל tells רב מנשיא to answer
steps.stepSummary: While the question was on its way, לוי died. שמואל told רב מנשיא that if he was wise enough, he should send the answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: While it was going, לוי passed away. שמואל said to רב מנשיא: If you are wise, send them an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the next move. It explains why רב מנשיא, and not לוי, gives the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questions were addressed to לוי, but he died before they arrived. שמואל passes the job to רב מנשיא, which tells us these answers come from רב מנשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: While it was going (on the way)
He passed away (literally, his soul rested)

phrases.english: While it was on its way, Levi passed away.
Shmuel said to Rav Menashya:
If you are wise, send them an answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrative bridge explaining who answers the questions of Step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This step only hands the questions to רב מנשיא.

steps.title: There is no permitted way to set up a canopy
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא answers the first question. They checked every possible way of setting up a כילה on שבת and found no permitted way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent them: A canopy — we went around all sides of the canopy and did not find for it a permitted side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא answers the first of the three questions, about the canopy. His answer is that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'We went around all sides' means they looked at every way one might spread a canopy on שבת. Every way counts as making a tent, so there is no way to permit it. The other two questions are answered in the next lines.
steps.confusionAlert: This answers only the first question. The answers about hops and about someone who dies on יום טוב continue next.

phrases.english: He sent them:

phrases.aramaic: כִּילָּה — חָזַרְנוּ עַל כׇּל צִידֵּי כִּילָּה
phrases.english: A canopy — we went around all the sides of the canopy
and did not find any permitted side to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: כִּילָּה — חָזַרְנוּ עַל כׇּל צִידֵּי כִּילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first question from Step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Spreading a כילה on שבת has no permitted way. It is forbidden.

steps.title: Why not send them the leniency of רמי בר יחזקאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב מנשיא did not tell them about the permitted way to set up a כילה taught by רמי בר יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him send them the ruling of רמי בר יחזקאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מנשיא's first answer. He said there is no permitted way to set up a כילה on שבת, but רמי בר יחזקאל taught a way that is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מנשיא's answer sounded like a total ban. The גמרא points out that a known opinion does allow a certain way of setting it up. So why did he leave that out?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him send them (a challenge: why didn't he?)
An אמורא who taught a permitted way to set up a canopy on שבת

phrases.english: And let him send them
phrases.notes: The גמרא is pushing back: he should have just told them.

phrases.english: according to Rami bar Yeḥezkel!
phrases.notes: רמי בר יחזקאל had a lenient method for a כילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב מנשיא's answer about the כילה from Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשיא's claim that there is no permitted way to set up a כילה on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known opinion, that of רמי בר יחזקאל, does allow a certain method. So the full answer should have included it.

steps.title: They were not learned in Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא held back the leniency because the people of בשכר were not learned and might confuse a permitted method with a forbidden one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב מנשיא kept the leniency to himself on purpose. The people were not learned enough to use it correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה does have a lenient method, but teaching it to people who are not careful could lead them to do the forbidden kind as well. So he gave them a stricter answer to protect them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a teacher may hold back a true leniency when the audience might misuse it.

phrases.english: Because they are not people of Torah.
phrases.notes: They would not tell the permitted method apart from the forbidden one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical or policy reason: the leniency was held back on purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מנשיא should have taught every halachic option, including רמי בר יחזקאל's leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: He deliberately left out the leniency because the questioners were not learned and might misapply it.

steps.title: Hops in a vineyard are a forbidden mixture
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא answers the second question: hops in a vineyard count as כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hops in a vineyard are a forbidden mixture.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא answers the second question from בשכר. Planting hops in a vineyard is forbidden as כלאי הכרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second of the three answers. It treats hops like any food crop that may not be sown among grapevines.

keyTerms.meaning: Hops (a climbing plant used in brewing)

phrases.english: Hops in a vineyard —
are a forbidden mixture.
phrases.notes: This means כלאי הכרם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to רב מנשיא's answer to the second question asked in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May hops be sown in a vineyard?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. It is a forbidden mixture (כלאים).

steps.title: Why not follow the lenient view of רבי טרפון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he did not permit hops, since רבי טרפון says hops are not כלאים, and outside ארץ ישראל we follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him send them the view of רבי טרפון! For it was taught: about hops, רבי טרפון says they are not כלאים in a vineyard, and the חכמים say they are. And we hold that whoever is lenient in the Land, the הלכה follows him outside the Land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer about hops. It quotes a dispute and a rule that seem to make hops permitted in בבל, where בשכר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the halacha follows the חכמים against רבי טרפון. But כלאים outside ארץ ישראל is only rabbinic, so we follow whoever is lenient. That means hops should be allowed there.

keyTerms.meaning: תנא who rules that hops are not כלאים
Forbidden mixtures of crops in a vineyard
And we hold as an established rule

phrases.english: And let him send them according to Rabbi Tarfon?
As it was taught: Hops —
Rabbi Tarfon says:
They are not a forbidden mixture in a vineyard.
And the Sages say: They are a forbidden mixture in a vineyard.
And we hold:
Anyone who is lenient in the Land [of Israel],
the halacha follows him outside the Land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer about hops from Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that hops in a vineyard are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון permits hops. Outside ארץ ישראל the lenient view in כלאים is followed, so in בבל hops should be permitted.

steps.title: Again: they were not learned in Torah
steps.stepSummary: Same answer: he held back the leniency because the people were not learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. רב מנשיא did not want to teach a leniency to unlearned people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hops really may be permitted in בבל, but unlearned people might stretch that permission to other plants that are truly forbidden. So he answered strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not learned in Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Both times, רב מנשיא hid a real leniency, about the כילה and about hops, because the people of בשכר were not learned and might misuse it.

phrases.english: Because they are not people of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 the same way Step 25 answered Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical or policy reason: the leniency was held back on purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should have permitted hops according to רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency is real, but he did not reveal it to unlearned people.

steps.title: רב announces that hops may be sown in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב publicly announced that anyone who wants to sow hops in a vineyard may do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would announce: Whoever wants to sow hops in a vineyard, let him sow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story. רב acted on the leniency openly and announced it to the public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the rule from Step 27 that outside ארץ ישראל we follow רבי טרפון's lenient view. Unlike רב מנשיא, רב made the permission public.

phrases.english: Rav would announce:
Whoever wants
to sow hops in a vineyard —
let him sow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the leniency of Step 27 put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sowing hops in a vineyard is permitted (in בבל).

steps.title: רב עמרם חסידא gives lashes for it
steps.stepSummary: In contrast, רב עמרם חסידא punished people with lashes for sowing hops in a vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם חסידא would give lashes for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the opposite practice. רב עמרם חסידא treated sowing hops in a vineyard as forbidden and punished it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He followed the חכמים, who say hops are כלאים. Since it is only rabbinic outside ארץ ישראל, the lashes were rabbinic lashes (מכת מרדות).

keyTerms.meaning: For it, on account of it

phrases.english: Rav Amram the Pious
would administer lashes for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practice opposite to רב's in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sowing hops in a vineyard is punished, so it is treated as forbidden.

steps.title: רב משרשיא has a non-Jewish child sow hops
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא paid a פרוטה to a non-Jewish child, who sowed the hops for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא would give a פרוטה to a non-Jewish child, and the child sowed for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a middle path. רב משרשיא did not sow the hops himself. He paid a non-Jewish child to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wanted the hops in his vineyard but avoided doing the questionable act himself. The next steps explain why he picked this kind of helper.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya would give
a peruta to a gentile child
and he would sow for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ פְּרוּטָה לְתִינוֹק גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third approach, between רב and רב עמרם חסידא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hops were sown for him through a non-Jewish child.

steps.title: Why not a Jewish child?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he did not use a Jewish child, who is also not obligated in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him give it to a Jewish child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions his choice. A Jewish child is not yet obligated either, so why insist on a non-Jew?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only goal was to have someone not obligated do the act, a Jewish child would seem to work just as well.

phrases.english: And let him give it to a Jewish child!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב משרשיא's choice in Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: His choice of a non-Jewish child
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jewish minor is also not obligated, so he should be an equally good choice.

steps.title: He might keep the habit
steps.stepSummary: A Jewish child might get used to it and keep doing it as an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will come to continue the habit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a Jewish child could form a habit. Then he might keep sowing hops in vineyards when he grows up and is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is not the child's act now but his future. A non-Jewish child has no such risk, because he will never be bound by this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to get used to it (form a habit)

phrases.english: He will come to continue the habit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A Jewish child is just as suitable as a non-Jewish child.
steps.terutzMaskana: A Jewish child might continue the practice as an adult.

steps.title: Why not a non-Jewish adult?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he did not hire a non-Jewish adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him give it to a non-Jewish adult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. A non-Jewish adult has no habit problem, so why specifically a child?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 33 rules out Jewish children only. It does not explain why he avoided non-Jewish adults.

phrases.english: And let him give it to an adult gentile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up challenge after Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: His choice of a child rather than an adult non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A non-Jewish adult has no habit problem, so he should work just as well.

steps.title: People might mistake him for a Jew
steps.stepSummary: Onlookers might think a non-Jewish adult is a Jew and conclude that Jews may sow hops.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will come to be confused with a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that people seeing an adult sowing might think he is Jewish. They would then learn the wrong lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a child, people understand that a minor is not bound by the rules. With an adult, onlookers might assume a Jewish adult is doing it, and they would copy him. So a non-Jewish child is the only safe choice.
steps.whatToRemember: רב משרשיא chose a non-Jewish child carefully. A Jewish child might form a habit, and a non-Jewish adult might be mistaken for a Jew.

phrases.english: He will come to be confused with a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 34 and closes the discussion of רב משרשיא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A non-Jewish adult would be an acceptable helper.
steps.terutzMaskana: Onlookers might mistake him for a Jew and learn the wrong הלכה.

steps.title: No one may bury a person who died on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The answer about a מת: neither Jews nor non-Jews may handle his burial, on either the first or the second day of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a dead person, he sent them this answer: If a person died on יום טוב, neither Jews nor non-Jews should handle his burial. This applies on the first day of יום טוב and on the second day of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next answer in the list of questions from בשכר. This one is about someone who died on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is very strict. Not even a non-Jew (ארמאי) may do the burial work, and the ban covers even יום טוב שני, which is only a rabbinic day kept outside ארץ ישראל. The next step will question this strictness.

keyTerms.meaning: Handle him, meaning take care of his burial
The second day of יום טוב, kept outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the hops answer from earlier. There, a non-Jewish child was allowed to do the work. Here, the answer says that even non-Jews may not do it.

phrases.english: About a dead person, he sent them:
phrases.notes: This continues the series of answers to the people of בשכר.

phrases.english: A dead person, they should not handle him
phrases.notes: This means they should not take care of his burial on יום טוב.

phrases.english: neither Jews nor Arameans (non-Jews),
neither on the first day of the Festival
nor on the second day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the hops answer (Steps 31-35) to the next answer in the same list, about a מת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who died on יום טוב may not be buried by Jews or by non-Jews, on either the first or the second day of יום טוב.

steps.title: A challenge from an incident in the shul of מעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this ruling is correct, and begins quoting רבי אסי's story about a death in מעון on a יום טוב next to שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי יהודה בר שילת said in the name of רבי אסי: There was an incident in the shul of מעון on a יום טוב that was right next to שבת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from Step 36 by starting to tell a story. This step only sets up the challenge. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אִינִי signals that a source is about to contradict the strict ruling. The story is set on a יום טוב next to שבת, which would mean two days in a row without burial. That setting suggests the story will show a more lenient ruling about burial.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" It opens a challenge.
A יום טוב right next to שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished yet. This passage stops in the middle of the story, and the actual contradiction (what was done with the מת) comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is surprised and pushing back here.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehuda bar Sheilat say
that Rabbi Asi said:
There was an incident in the synagogue of Maon
on a Festival adjacent to Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר שִׁילַת אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the strict burial ruling of Step 36 using a story passed down by רבי אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that nobody, not even non-Jews, may bury a מת on either day of יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story about a death on a יום טוב next to שבת is introduced as a source that apparently contradicts the strict ruling. The details are completed on the next amud.
